newsitem.title: UK: Jeddah inquiry new first on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Jeddah inquiry new first on sugar freight market.

text.p: New business was brisk on the sugar freight market on Tuesday with one route quoted by a charterer for the first time ever, shipbrokers said. CSR scored a new first with an inquiry to ship 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Jeddah for 10/20 November.
"It's their first ever (to Jeddah). I believe the size is likely to increase next year when the new refinery gets going," one shipbroker said.
Saudi Arabia's new refinery at Jeddah is expected to come on stream in early 1997 and should take around 450,000 tonnes of raw sugar for refining throughout the year.
Jean Lion featured twice with tonnage to ship prompt cargoes of bagged sugar from Continent to Algeria. Shipbrokers said it fixed 4,000 tonnes and was in the market for a further 5/6,000.
Other new business came from E D & F Man, which quoted for 6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from north France to Syria for 24/28 October.
Fiji Sugar Marketing was open for 15,000 tonnes in bulk from Fiji to Japan for 10/20 November, and shipbrokers said the rate likely to be achieved was in the region of $22.00.
Cargill fixed a prompt 14,000-tonne bulk cargo from Maceio or Recife to Morocco with Egyptian Mediterranean and Black Sea options. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.
Shipbrokers cited market talk that Mauritius Sugar Syndicate was close to fixing 14,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London for October/November shipment dates.
